summary: A worst-case valid string can hide its decisive third mismatch at the final inspected mirrored pair, giving an Omega(n) inspection lower bound matched by the two-pointer scan.

optimality.argument: For strings whose first floor(n/2)-1 mirrored pairs contain at most two mismatches, changing only the last uninspected mirrored character can switch the answer by creating or removing a third mismatch. A correct worst-case algorithm must therefore inspect a linear number of positions, and the submitted scan does so once.

replacement_checks.evidence: An adversary can keep the outcome undecided until the innermost mirrored pair by placing the possible third mismatch there.
The implementation performs one constant-time comparison for each mirrored pair and stops no later than the third mismatch.
Authored cases cover lengths one and two, zero through three mismatches, odd and even palindromes, and a late third mismatch.
